Playbook.name: QA - Potential Unauthorized Changes - SOC Playbook

Technique.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify System Firewall

Reference.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1562.004 Disable or Modify System Firewall

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A configuration change was made on a FortiGate firewall (action Add/Edit/Delete on a system/firewall object — verified live: fortinet.firewall.cfgpath e.g. "firewall.policy", with the exact attribute delta in fortinet.firewall.cfgattr). The triage question: is this an authorised, change-managed edit by a network administrator, or an unauthorised/attacker modification that weakens the firewall (opens a policy, changes an address object, alters admin access)? IMPORTANT JCB TELEMETRY NOTES (verified live): on config-change events user.name and source.ip are NULL — the actor is carried in fortinet.firewall.ui, which reads like "GUI(192.168.193.10)" (admin via GUI from that source IP), "jsconsole", or "ha_daemon". "ha_daemon" is the High-Availability cluster automatically replicating the change from the primary to the secondary member (JCB-FGT-Primary/JCB-FGT-Secondary) and is benign. The field fortinet.firewall.msg does NOT exist in this data — use cfgpath/cfgattr/ui.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: The FortiGate cluster is the perimeter and internal segmentation control for the bank's internet-facing and internal services. An unauthorised change — opening a policy, weakening an address group, altering admin/trusted-host settings — can expose banking applications or create a durable ingress path. Config changes made outside change control are the ones to scrutinise.

Assets.AssetType: FortiGate firewall cluster (JCB-FGT-Primary / JCB-FGT-Secondary — perimeter and segmentation)

LogSources.LogSource: FortiGate event log — logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* (verified live: fortinet.firewall.action Add/Edit/Delete, cfgpath, cfgattr, ui, observer.name; user.name/source.ip null on config events)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: FortiGate admin/config event logging shipped to logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* (verified live: Add/Edit/Delete on subtype "system" with cfgpath/cfgattr populated).

ACTOR IS IN ui, NOT user.name: on config-change events user.name and source.ip are null (verified live). Read the operator from fortinet.firewall.ui — "GUI(<ip>)" gives the admin's source IP; "ha_daemon" is benign HA replication between cluster members.

Changes appear in PAIRS across the cluster: the member where the admin acted shows ui="GUI(<ip>)"; the peer shows the same change with ui="ha_daemon" (verified live). Do not double-count the HA copy as a second unauthorised change.

Signal.Name: Firewall config change
Signal.Details: fortinet.firewall.action Add/Edit/Delete with cfgpath (object type) and cfgattr (the attribute delta) on a FortiGate (observer.name).

Signal.Name: Operator origin
Signal.Details: fortinet.firewall.ui identifies the operator: GUI(<ip>)/jsconsole = a human/admin session from that source; ha_daemon = automatic cluster replication (benign).

Input.name: $observer
Input.description: The FortiGate device the change was logged on (observer.name from the alert, e.g. JCB-FGT-Primary).

ImmediateCapture.Item: What changed: cfgpath (object) and cfgattr (attribute delta) from the alert
Operator origin: fortinet.firewall.ui — GUI(<ip>) vs ha_daemon vs jsconsole/console

InitialAssessment.Rule: If the change ui is "ha_daemon", it is the HA peer replicating an edit already made on the other member — investigate the originating member, do not treat the replica as a separate change.

If ui is "GUI(<known-admin-ip>)" during a change window with a ticket, lean authorised administration. An unfamiliar source IP in ui, or a change to admin-access/trusted-host/policy that opens exposure with no ticket, escalates.

Investigation.Goal: Decide whether the FortiGate configuration change on $observer is authorised, change-managed administration or an unauthorised/attacker modification, attributing the operator via fortinet.firewall.ui and separating genuine edits from benign HA replication.

Step.name: Summarise the changes by operator on the device
Step.Purpose: Group the config changes on $observer by action and operator (ui) — this immediately separates human/admin edits (GUI/jsconsole) from benign HA replication (ha_daemon) and shows what object types were touched.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* | WHERE observer.name == "$observer" AND fortinet.firewall.action IN ("Add","Edit","Delete") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL actor = fortinet.firewall.ui | STATS changes = COUNT(*), paths = VALUES(fortinet.firewall.cfgpath), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY fortinet.firewall.action, actor | SORT changes DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: ha_daemon rows are the cluster peer replicating a change made on the other member — benign; pivot to the originating member. GUI(<ip>)/jsconsole rows are the real operator sessions to assess. An unfamiliar source IP inside a GUI(...) value is the standout signal.

Step.name: Inspect exactly what was changed
Step.Purpose: Read the concrete attribute deltas (cfgattr) per object (cfgpath) so the security impact of the change is understood — e.g. a policy opened, an address object widened, admin access altered.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* | WHERE observer.name == "$observer" AND fortinet.firewall.action IN ("Add","Edit","Delete") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, fortinet.firewall.action, fortinet.firewall.cfgpath, fortinet.firewall.cfgattr, fortinet.firewall.ui | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 30
Step.AnalystNotes: Judge impact from cfgpath+cfgattr: changes to firewall.policy (allow rules), address/address-group objects that widen scope, system.admin / system.api-user, or admin trusted-host/interface access are the high-impact cases. Housekeeping edits (logging, comments, unrelated objects) are lower-impact. cfgattr shows the before->after values.

Step.name: Enumerate every operator that changed config (HA vs human)
Step.Purpose: List all distinct operators (ui) that made changes and how many, so a single unexpected operator among the routine HA/admin traffic is obvious.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* | WHERE observer.name == "$observer" AND fortinet.firewall.action IN ("Add","Edit","Delete") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL is_ha = fortinet.firewall.ui LIKE "ha_daemon*" | STATS changes = COUNT(*), objects = COUNT_DISTINCT(fortinet.firewall.cfgpath), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY fortinet.firewall.ui, is_ha | SORT changes DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Expect a small set: ha_daemon (benign replica) and one or two known admin GUI(<mgmt-ip>) values. Any additional operator — an unfamiliar GUI source IP, an API user, or a console session at an odd time — is the one to justify against change control.

Step.name: Correlate an admin login/session to the change
Step.Purpose: Tie the change to an administrative login on the device — a login from the same source in the window supports an attributable human change; changes with no corresponding admin login are more suspicious.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* | WHERE observer.name == "$observer" AND fortinet.firewall.action == "login" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS logins = COUNT(*), users = VALUES(user.name), sources = VALUES(source.ip), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY event.outcome | SORT logins DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A successful admin login from the same source IP embedded in the change's GUI(...) ui, by a known admin account, corroborates authorised administration. Failed logins before the change (event.outcome != success) or a change with no admin login session at all raises the likelihood of unauthorised/automated tampering.

Node.Condition: INV-02/INV-03 show a high-impact change (firewall.policy opened, address object widened, system.admin/api-user or admin trusted-host/access altered) by an unfamiliar operator (unknown GUI source IP or unexpected API/console session) with no change ticket.
Node.Result: True Positive (Unauthorised firewall change weakening defenses — escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-04 shows the change coincides with failed admin logins or has no corresponding admin login session, and the operator origin cannot be tied to an authorised admin.
Node.Result: True Positive (Suspicious/unattributable configuration change — escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01/INV-03 show the change was made by a known admin from a recognised management IP (GUI(<mgmt-ip>)) during a change window, INV-04 corroborates the admin login, and the change maps to a ticket.
The only records are ha_daemon replicas of a change already assessed on the originating cluster member (no new human edit).
An API/automation operator (ui) made a legitimate-intent, scoped change matching a known workflow but outside the change-control path.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (Automation acting off change-control — route it through change control, do not blanket-exception)

Node.Condition: Operator origin is a known admin but no ticket/change record can be found, or the change impact is unclear.

FalsePositive.Definition: The change was authorised, change-managed administration by a known network admin, OR it is the HA peer benignly replicating a change already assessed on the other cluster member. "Authorised" or "proven HA replication" — never merely "a config changed".

Indicators.Item: ui = GUI(<recognised management IP>) by a known admin during an approved change window (INV-01/INV-03), corroborated by an admin login (INV-04).
ui = ha_daemon and the originating member's change is itself benign/authorised.
cfgattr shows a low-impact/housekeeping edit consistent with the ticket.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the change ticket and operator; close as false_positive.
For ha_daemon records, reference the originating member's assessment; do not raise a duplicate.

TruePositive.Definition: An unauthorised or attacker-driven change weakened the firewall — opening a policy, widening an address object, or altering administrative access — outside change control.

Indicators.Item: High-impact cfgpath/cfgattr change (policy/address/system.admin/trusted-host) by an unfamiliar operator (unknown GUI source IP, unexpected API/console).
No corresponding authorised admin login, or failed logins preceding the change (INV-04).
No change ticket; timing outside maintenance windows.

SOCAction.Item: Engage network/firewall admins to confirm and, if unauthorised, revert the change; preserve the config revision.
Treat the operator source as suspect; review FortiGate admin accounts and trusted-host settings; hunt for follow-on access enabled by the change.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An automation/orchestration account (or an admin using an unsanctioned method) made a legitimate-intent change outside the change-control path — operational, not malicious.

Indicators.Item: An API/automation ui makes recurring, scoped changes matching a known workflow.
Owner confirms the automation and its scope.

SOCAction.Item: Route the automation through change control; document its expected cfgpath scope; keep the analytic enabled.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: From INV-02 determine the security impact of the change; from INV-01/INV-03 attribute the operator (ui) and discount ha_daemon replicas.
If the change is high-impact and unattributable/unauthorised, engage firewall admins to revert it and preserve the current and prior config revisions.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Revert the unauthorised change; review adjacent config (policies, address objects, admin accounts, trusted hosts) for further tampering.
If an operator source is suspect, rotate FortiGate admin credentials/API keys and restrict admin access (trusted hosts); hunt for access enabled by the change.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce change control for FortiGate edits; restrict admin GUI/API to defined management IPs; enable config-change notification/backup.
Baseline the expected operator (ui) set per member and alert on any new operator or high-impact cfgpath change as a higher-severity analytic.

Escalation.Trigger: High-impact change (policy/address/admin access) by an unfamiliar operator, a change with no authorised admin login or preceded by failed logins, or an unrevertable/unexplained modification.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Change verified against an approved ticket and a known admin operator, or confirmed as a benign HA replica of an assessed change.
cfgattr impact reviewed and consistent with the authorised intent.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Unauthorised change reverted and config revision preserved; adjacent config reviewed for further tampering.
Suspect operator/credentials contained and rotated; follow-on access hunted; incident documented.
